semantic_anchor: 02A section 1 - Character coverage or word efficiency?
prompt: Minimal but graphic-rich educational poster, landscape 16:9. Warm, friendly pets-at-home feel: cream paper background, rounded flat paper cards in teal, orange and purple, navy large sans-serif text, every word crisp and legible. Small flat cartoon illustrations of a ginger cat and a brown dog where described, plus a few paw-print or yarn-ball doodles in the margins only. Title 'Three ways to cut up a new word'. Top left: a small sticky note with a sleepy cartoon cat curled up, and the word 'sleepyhead' written on the note. Below, THREE horizontal lanes stacked with whitespace, each with a heading card on the left. Lane 1 heading 'Letters': exactly ten small teal tiles in order 's' 'l' 'e' 'e' 'p' 'y' 'h' 'e' 'a' 'd', then a note 'Never stuck, but long'. Lane 2 heading 'Whole words': one tile 'sleepyhead' with a red dashed outline and a red question mark, then a note 'Short, but stuck on new words'. Lane 3 heading 'Reusable pieces (BPE)': one wide green tile 'sleepy' followed by four small teal tiles 'h' 'e' 'a' 'd', then a note 'Known piece + spare letters'. Footer 'Keep the letters as a safety net. Glue the common bits together.'
acceptance_criteria: Exactly three lanes; letters lane has the ten letters of sleepyhead in order; words lane shows sleepyhead as unknown; BPE lane shows sleepy then h e a d.
prohibited_content: Photographic animals, extra words on cards, misspelled labels, tiny unreadable text, equations, invented numbers or charts, logos.
alt_text: The new word sleepyhead split three ways: ten single letters, one unknown whole word, or the learned piece sleepy plus the letters h, e, a, d.

semantic_anchor: 02A section 3 - Token IDs address static rows
prompt: Minimal but graphic-rich educational poster, landscape 16:9. Warm, friendly pets-at-home feel: cream paper background, rounded flat paper cards in teal, orange and purple, navy large sans-serif text, every word crisp and legible. Small flat cartoon illustrations of a ginger cat and a brown dog where described, plus a few paw-print or yarn-ball doodles in the margins only. Title 'An ID is a drawer number, not a meaning'. Left: a teal card with a small cartoon cat and the text ' cat'. Arrow to an orange name-tag card 'ID 3797'. Arrow to a tall wooden chest of many small drawers labelled 'GPT-2 table: 50,257 drawers', with one drawer pulled open labelled 'drawer 3797'. From the open drawer, an arrow to a purple card holding a row of eight coloured vertical bars of different heights with NO numbers, labelled 'one row of learnable numbers'. Bottom panel separated by whitespace, heading 'Same word, same drawer': two small speech-bubble cards 'the loud bark woke the cat' (tiny barking dog doodle) and 'the rough bark covered the tree' (tiny tree doodle), both with arrows into ONE shared drawer labelled 'bark'. Note beside it 'The sentence, not the drawer, says which bark.' Footer 'Lookup fetches a row. Later layers mix in context.'
acceptance_criteria: ' cat' to ID 3797 to drawer 3797 to an unlabelled bar row; 50,257 drawers label; both bark sentences point to one bark drawer.
prohibited_content: Photographic animals, extra words on cards, misspelled labels, tiny unreadable text, equations, invented numbers or charts, logos. Numbers on the bars, different drawers for the two barks, suggesting the ID size means anything.
alt_text: The piece ' cat' gets ID 3797, which opens drawer 3797 in GPT-2's table of 50,257 drawers and fetches one row of learnable numbers. Both meanings of bark open the same drawer.

prompt: Minimal but graphic-rich educational poster, landscape 16:9. Top: a batch drawn as a grid of exactly TWO rows and FIVE columns of rounded cells. Row 1: teal cells 'the' 'cat' 'sat', then two grey dashed cells 'pad' 'pad'. Row 2: teal cells 'the' 'dog', then three grey dashed cells 'pad' 'pad' 'pad'. A small note 'Shorter notes get blank seats so the batch is a rectangle'. Bottom: two side-by-side panels. Left panel with a red border, heading 'Average every cell': the whole grid highlighted including the grey cells, a red cross, note 'Blank seats water down the score'. alt_text: A two-row batch, 'the cat sat' and 'the dog', padded to five seats. Averaging every cell lets blanks water down the score; averaging only real words keeps it honest.

semantic_anchor: 02B section 3 - Random rows can identify words. Can we make them more useful?
prompt: Minimal but graphic-rich educational poster, landscape 16:9. Warm, friendly pets-at-home feel: cream paper background, rounded flat paper cards in teal, orange and purple, navy large sans-serif text, every word crisp and legible. Small flat cartoon illustrations of a ginger cat and a brown dog where described, plus a few paw-print or yarn-ball doodles in the margins only. Title 'Practice nudges the drawer you opened'. TWO separate panels divided by whitespace. Top panel heading '1. Make a guess'. Left: a small cabinet of three drawers 'cat' (tiny cat doodle), 'dog' (tiny dog doodle), 'bird' (tiny bird doodle); only the cat drawer is pulled open and glowing teal; dog and bird are closed and grey. Then navy arrows left to right: purple card 'row of numbers' with unlabelled bars, purple card 'predictor', card 'guess' with four short bars labelled 'sat', 'slept', 'flew', 'sang' and no numbers. prohibited_content: Photographic animals, extra words on cards, misspelled labels, tiny unreadable text, equations, invented numbers or charts, logos. Feedback arrows to the dog or bird drawers, percentages.
alt_text: Opening the cat drawer fetches its row; the predictor makes a shortlist of sat, slept, flew and sang. Comparing with the answer sat updates only the cat row and the predictor weights; dog and bird rows are unchanged.

semantic_anchor: 02B section 4 - Pad the batch, then prove padding contributes zero loss
prompt: Minimal but graphic-rich educational poster, landscape 16:9. Warm, friendly pets-at-home feel: cream paper background, rounded flat paper cards in teal, orange and purple, navy large sans-serif text, every word crisp and legible. Small flat cartoon illustrations of a ginger cat and a brown dog where described, plus a few paw-print or yarn-ball doodles in the margins only. Title 'Two honest ways to skip blank seats'. Top centre: a batch grid of exactly THREE rows and THREE columns. Row 1: teal 'the' 'cat' 'sat'. Row 2: teal 'the' 'dog', grey dashed 'pad'. Row 3: teal 'bird', grey dashed 'pad' 'pad'. Small caption '6 real words, 3 blank seats'. Below, THREE text-only panels side by side, no mini grids inside them. Panel 1 red border, red cross, text 'Average all 9 cells' and 'Blank seats sneak in'. Panel 2 green border, green tick, text 'Mask: add up the 6 real cells, divide by 6'. Panel 3 green border, green tick, text 'ignore_index = pad' and 'PyTorch skips them for you'. Below panels 2 and 3 only, one green card 'Same answer' with exactly TWO green arrows into it, one from panel 2 and one from panel 3. Panel 1 has no arrow. A small cartoon dog sits in the bottom-left corner away from text.
acceptance_criteria: Grid 3 by 3 with bird as a real teal word; panels contain only text; red panel unconnected; two green arrows into Same answer.
prohibited_content: Photographic animals, extra words on cards, misspelled labels, tiny unreadable text, equations, invented numbers or charts, logos. Loss values, a fourth row.
alt_text: A three-row batch with six real words and three blank seats. Averaging all nine cells is wrong; masking the blanks or using ignore_index both give the same correct answer.
